purpose: Case-driven verification plan for the Blackwell warp-specialization article. Every case names a frozen fixture and the strongest structural claim that can be made without SM103 execution.

maturity.compiler_core: Default pipeline or final lowering with direct focused coverage.
maturity.integrated_shape: Python or full-pipeline fixture demonstrates a recognized end-to-end input shape.
maturity.focused_shape: A dedicated MLIR unit fixture proves one transformation boundary.
maturity.experimental_shape: Implemented and tested but narrow, heuristic, or explicitly restricted.
maturity.negative_contract: Test proves that a tempting input does not trigger automatic specialization.

assertion.required: Must be checked and is supported by frozen source/test evidence.
assertion.forbidden: Must be absent for this case.
assertion.advisory: Useful observation only; exact spelling/count is toolchain-sensitive or not covered by the fixture.
assertion.not_applicable: The selected fixture intentionally stops before this representation.

evidence_kind.inference: Reasoned compile artifact expectation; never a runtime measurement.

recommended_artifacts: TTIR immediately after frontend code generation
TTGIR after each AutomaticWarpSpecialization subpass where the fixture supports it
LLVM-dialect MLIR before and after ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM
LLVM IR, PTX, and cubin when the local CUDA toolchain accepts sm_103
nvdisasm output only as a non-blocking advisory artifact
global_protocol.success_rule: Compile success and required structural checks establish implementation behavior; they do not establish numerical correctness, occupancy, latency hiding, or speedup.
global_protocol.sass_rule: No exact SASS mnemonic is a required assertion in compile-only mode. Record toolchain version and preserve output if available.

cases.title: Explicit ttg.warp_specialize: default path plus persistent worker switch loop
cases.objective: Start from an already explicit WS op and isolate the physical execution model without involving automatic partition policy.

source_fixtures.role: Small compile fixture containing explicit ttg.warp_specialize.
Focused FileCheck for worker state dispatch.
Capture transport, relative warp IDs, and control flow.

pipeline_checkpoints: AllocateWarpGroups pads worker topology and assigns warp IDs/register budgets.
SCF-to-CF and shared allocation make capture/state storage concrete.
ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM lowers the explicit op through lowerWarpSpecializeCommon.

ir.pattern: ttg.warp_specialize before final WS lowering
worker shared-state load, switch/branch dispatch, partition body, return-to-dispatch loop, and exit state after lowering
default and worker barrier synchronization; relative worker warp IDs

ptx.pattern: CTA named-barrier synchronization or bar.warp.sync for a one-warp participant, plus shared state loads/stores and branch targets

sass.pattern: Control-flow loop and barrier instructions corresponding to the PTX state machine

cases.maturity_note: Final WS lowering is a compiler core. This case proves mechanism, not that autoWS can discover the partition.
limitations: No runtime overlap or efficiency conclusion is permitted.

pipeline_checkpoints: AllocateWarpGroups before shared/TMEM allocation.

TMemBarrierInsertion orders overlapping TMEM accesses.

TensorMemoryLoad/Store/Copy converted to target intrinsics

ptx.pattern: tcgen05.ld, tcgen05.st, tcgen05.cp, and/or tcgen05.wait according to the selected fixture

sass.pattern: TMEM load/store/copy instruction family corresponding to emitted PTX

cases.maturity_note: TMEM lowering and explicit WS are core; exact allocation shape remains target/layout dependent.
limitations: The micro-IR bypasses automatic partition discovery.

cases.title: One TMA operand plus one ordinary async-copy operand
cases.category: automatic WS plus ordinary software pipeline
cases.objective: Prove that autoWS can specialize the eligible descriptor path while ordinary async copy remains in the surrounding pipeline.

source_fixtures.role: Parameterized end-to-end kernel with one TMA and one ordinary load.

pipeline_checkpoints: PartitionScheduling sees eligible descriptor memory and TCGen05 MMA roots.
InsertAref/LowerAref protocolize the TMA-produced shared tile.
Pipeline materializes the remaining ordinary async-copy stages after autoWS.
OptimizePartitionWarps sizes the resulting workers.

sass.pattern: Both tensor-map transfer and ordinary copy instruction families around tensor-core work

cases.maturity_note: This mixed shape has focused and Python integration coverage; performance overlap remains unmeasured.

cases.title: Canonical TMA autoWS GEMM
cases.objective: Use the smallest representative frontend case to follow the complete mechanism from tl.range to TCGen05/PTX.

source_fixtures.role: Integration assertions for TCGen05, TMA, and ttg.warp_specialize.

pipeline_checkpoints: CodeGenerator.visit_For emits tt.warp_specialize.
PartitionScheduling forms load and MMA/TMEM partitions.
InsertAref and InsertTmemAref remove cross-partition ownership edges.
LowerAref -> PartitionLoops -> LowerWarpGroup creates ttg.warp_specialize.
Pipeline/OptimizePartitionWarps and LLIR resource allocation finalize worker topology.
ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM and MMAv5/TMEM conversions form PTX-ready IR.

sass.pattern: Tensor-map transfer, tensor-core/TMEM, barrier, and possible USETMAXREG-class instructions

cases.title: Nested persistent GEMM with TCGen05 and TMEM-clear hoisting
cases.objective: Trace the extra transformations required when one program persistently claims multiple output tiles.
pipeline_checkpoints: FuseNestedLoops, LICM, accumulator-init optimization, and first TMEM hoist prepare the persistent nest.
NVWSHoistTmemStore checks useD=false and trip/execution safety.
AutoWS partitions the inner compute/load schedule without breaking outer persistent iteration.
Second HoistTmemAlloc allows movement through if regions after pipelining.

passes.pattern: fuse_nested_loops -> LICM -> optimize_accumulator_init -> hoist_tmem_alloc(false) -> autoWS(NVWSHoistTmemStore included) -> pipeline -> hoist_tmem_alloc(true)

ir.pattern: Outer persistent tile loop retained with inner ttg.warp_specialize work
Redundant TMEM clear removed/folded only for the proven-safe pattern

ptx.pattern: Persistent outer control flow plus TMA mbarrier protocol, tcgen05.mma/commit, TMEM ops, and WS state machine

sass.pattern: Repeated tile-claim/control sequence surrounding transfer and tensor-core groups

cases.maturity_note: Integrated test coverage exists, but persistent nesting adds recognized-shape and hoisting constraints.
limitations: A failed hoist match is expected to retain extra clear/synchronization cost.
No persistent scheduling efficiency claim without runtime counters.

cases.title: Shared/register ARef producer-consumer protocol
cases.objective: Inspect the correctness bridge between a TMA-producing partition and one or more consumers before loop cloning.
pipeline_checkpoints: InsertAref replaces raw cross-partition SSA with aref.create and put/get enter/exit.
SCCP/CSE simplify the protocol.
LowerAref creates empty/full barriers and multibuffered shared storage.
PartitionLoops can then clone partitions without unresolved SSA dependencies.

passes.pattern: InsertAref -> verifier -> SCCP -> verifier -> CSE -> verifier -> LowerAref

ir.pattern: nvws.aref.create and matching put/get enter/exit after InsertAref
descriptor load converted to NVWS descriptor producer with transaction count
empty/full barrier waits and arrives plus numStages-controlled buffers after LowerAref

ptx.pattern: not applicable to InsertAref/LowerAref focused fixtures

cases.maturity_note: Broad focused coverage across shared, register, scalar, multiple, and conditional consumers.
limitations: ARef op syntax is transient compiler IR, not a stable user interface.

cases.title: TMEM ARef ownership transfer between MMA and consumer partitions
cases.objective: Follow asynchronous TCGen05 accumulator ownership without treating TMEM as ordinary shared memory.
pipeline_checkpoints: TmemAccessDag follows async tokens and overlapping accesses.
InsertTmemAref detects producer/consumer partitions and inserts ownership protocol for at most two groups.
LowerAref realizes barriers; TMemBarrierInsertion later handles physical overlap dependencies.

passes.pattern: InsertTmemAref before LowerAref and PartitionLoops; TMemBarrierInsertion later in make_llir

ir.pattern: TMEM ARef tied to async-token access DAG and partition ownership changes
Ping-pong stage annotations only when double buffering is legal
Additional TMEM dependency barriers where physical accesses overlap

ptx.pattern: tcgen05.commit mbarrier plus tcgen05.ld/st/wait and corresponding mbarrier protocol in a full compilation

cases.maturity_note: Substantial focused coverage, but the ownership model is deliberately narrower than arbitrary multi-partition TMEM graphs.
limitations: At most two groups participate in the modeled ping-pong transfer.
Scaled paths require dedicated cases and handling.

cases.title: Worker warp-count optimization and dynamic register reallocation
cases.objective: Connect logical partitions to physical warp IDs, total warps, and setmaxnreg operations.

source_fixtures.role: Physical ID, padding, and register-budget assignment.
NVVM SetMaxRegister lowering and over-allocation behavior.

pipeline_checkpoints: OptimizePartitionWarps halves candidates subject to TMA/TMEM minima and estimated tensor register use.
AllocateWarpGroups pads all WS sites to a common topology and sets ttg.total-num-warps.
ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM emits register increase/decrease at path transitions.

passes.pattern: OptimizePartitionWarps in make_ttgir, then AllocateWarpGroups in make_llir, then ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM

ir.pattern: worker num_warps reduced only to operation-specific legal minimum
ttg.total-num-warps, physical warp IDs, requestedRegisters/actualRegisters, and module maxnreg
nvvm.setmaxregister increase/decrease unless disabled by instrumentation/safety path

ptx.pattern: setmaxnreg increase/decrease directive/instruction form supported by the selected PTX ISA

sass.pattern: USETMAXREG-class instruction if ptxas preserves dynamic register reallocation

limitations: 65536-register budget and 2x tensor estimate are compiler policy constants at this snapshot.
Do not infer achieved occupancy from requested register counts alone.

cases.objective: Cover the extra partition roots and ownership edges introduced by FP8/FP4 scale tensors.

source_fixtures.role: Scaled MMA partition roots with register/TMA scales.
tl.dot_scaled frontend context, not by itself an autoWS assertion.

pipeline_checkpoints: PartitionScheduling recognizes TCGen5MMAScaledOp and scale-producing loads.
InsertAref/InsertTmemAref protocolize scale tensors according to storage and ownership.
MMAv5 conversion constructs FP8/FP4 scale descriptors and emits block-scale TCGen05 variants.

passes.pattern: PartitionScheduling -> InsertAref -> InsertTmemAref -> LowerAref -> MMAv5 scaled conversion

ir.pattern: ttng.tc_gen5_mma_scaled as a data partition root
Separate scale operand ARef/TMEM flow where the scale producer crosses a partition

sass.pattern: Scaled tensor-core and scale-transfer instruction groups

cases.title: 2CTA TCGen05 with cluster barriers inside WS
cases.objective: Expose the extra cross-CTA correctness machinery layered over ordinary WS barriers.
pipeline_checkpoints: PlanCTA and CheckMatmulTwoCTA establish the multi-CTA shape.
ClusterBarrierAnalysis inserts cross-CTA synchronization and init synchronization.
ClusterBarrierMbarAllocator reserves two 16-byte slots and records offsets/count.
InitializeWSClusterBarriers initializes both slots and modulo-4 slot/parity state for all warps.

passes.pattern: check_matmul_two_cta -> proxy_fence_insertion -> to_llvmir(cluster insertion/init sync/mbar allocation) -> initialize_ws_cluster_barriers -> warp_specialize_to_llvm

ir.pattern: ttg.mbar_offset and ttg.ws_cluster_barrier_count allocation metadata
Two cluster-shared mbarrier slots, counter, low-bit slot selection, high-bit parity selection, and all-warp cluster synchronization

ptx.pattern: cluster.arrive/cluster.wait and mbarrier operations in shared::cluster address space

sass.pattern: Cluster barrier and 2CTA tensor-core/TMEM instruction families

cases.maturity_note: Focused compiler coverage is strong, but launch/runtime behavior and benefit remain hardware-dependent and untested here.
limitations: No claim about cluster residency, scheduling fairness, or performance on SM103.
Exact cluster/PTX spellings depend on PTX ISA/toolchain version.

cases.title: Persistent attention inner loop with multiple TMA/TMEM flows
cases.objective: Stress partition propagation, multiple descriptors, conditional dataflow, TMEM ownership, and persistent outer scheduling beyond dense GEMM.
pipeline_checkpoints: PartitionScheduling merges/duplicates graph nodes across QK, softmax state, PV, and descriptor flows.
InsertAref handles multiple TMA-produced shared values and scalar/control dependencies.
InsertTmemAref tracks MMAv5 accumulator ownership across QK/PV phases.
Persistent loop scheduling and descriptor multibuffering occur after WS formation.

passes.pattern: Complete AutomaticWarpSpecialization composite including both ARef passes, then pipeline and partition-warp optimization

ir.pattern: Multiple data partitions and ttg.warp_specialize nested under persistent work distribution
Distinct shared and TMEM ownership protocols for Q/K/V/accumulator flows
Temporary partition tags removed after the composite pass

ptx.pattern: Multiple TMA bulk tensor transfers, mbarrier stage protocols, TCGen05 MMA/commit/TMEM operations, and WS worker dispatch

sass.pattern: Interleaved transfer, tensor-core/TMEM, scalar softmax, and barrier/control instruction regions

cases.maturity_note: Realistic integration and focused pass fixtures exist; the shape is materially more fragile than canonical GEMM.
limitations: Compile success does not validate numerical softmax behavior or the effectiveness of QK/PV overlap.
Exact partition membership is heuristic and may evolve.

cases.title: Grouped TMA GEMM with dynamic per-group descriptors
cases.objective: Verify autoWS when descriptor selection and dimensions vary across a persistent group loop.

source_fixtures.role: Python integration fixture and ttg.warp_specialize assertion.

pipeline_checkpoints: Loop/prologue descriptor values survive partition scheduling and control-flow propagation.
Automatic WS forms load/compute partitions inside grouped work distribution.
multiBufferTMADescriptors creates numStages + 1 buffers for changing descriptors.
Internal partition/scheduling attributes are cleaned after reconstruction.

passes.pattern: PartitionScheduling -> ARef/TMEM-ARef -> LowerAref -> PartitionLoops -> LowerWarpGroup -> ScheduleLoops -> multiBufferTMADescriptors -> cleanup

ir.pattern: ttg.warp_specialize within grouped/persistent control flow
Dynamic descriptor selection preserved and descriptor storage multibuffered
No leaked internal partition attributes

ptx.pattern: Per-group address/descriptor control plus TMA mbarrier transfers, TCGen05 compute, and WS state

sass.pattern: Dynamic group-control instruction region surrounding TMA/tensor-core worker paths

cases.maturity_note: Both focused and Python integration fixtures exist; descriptor dynamism makes it a stronger breadth case than fixed GEMM.
limitations: No load-balance, cache behavior, or grouped-work scheduling efficiency claim is made.

deferred_runtime_work.reason: No SM103 Blackwell device is available in the current environment and the user requested disruptive runtime setup be deferred.
record_only: Run numerical correctness against a non-WS reference for GEMM, persistent GEMM, attention, and grouped GEMM.
Compare WS on/off latency distributions after controlling num_warps, num_stages, input shape, clock state, and warmup.
Collect achieved occupancy, registers/thread, shared memory, active warps, tensor-pipe utilization, TMA throughput, barrier stalls, scoreboard stalls, and eligible-warps-per-cycle.
Disassemble cubins with the exact CUDA toolkit used for PTX assembly and correlate SASS regions with the LLVM/PTX state machine.
Test 2CTA cluster launch/residency separately; do not mix its results into one-CTA WS conclusions.
prohibited_until_measured: A particular partition count is optimal.
Results from a different target prove SM103 behavior.
